videoTitle: ASML's Secret: Laser Tin 🤯 Chip Printing!

fullVoiceover: How do we print transistors smaller than a virus? It’s not ink, it’s physics! ASML’s Extreme UV machines are mind-bogglingly precise. Most think chip printing is like a fancy inkjet. But 90% don't grasp the insane engineering. We're talking 2-nanometer lines! ASML uses CO2 lasers to blast molten tin droplets. Twice! 50,000 times a second. This generates the Extreme UV light needed. But this isn't easy. Critical choke points include precise laser alignment, preventing tin splatter, and avoiding optic degradation on the mirrors. This ballet of light and liquid metal builds our future, one atomic layer at a time. An engineering marvel, leaving everyone still asking...
